messages:
Priya (AcmeHealth): We just ran a scale test and started getting intermittent 5xxs around 14:05 UTC. It's a POC (hosted) hitting redwood-13b at ~3.5k rps. Need help diagnosing — procurement is asking for uptime proof.
OpsBot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate on cluster poc-acme-02 — error_rate=18% over 1min, queue_depth=630
Luis (Eng): Can you share a sample request id and whether you see client retries? Any payloads that are large?
Priya (AcmeHealth): sample id req_a9c1d. Calls are standard chat completions, avg tokens in=120, out=400. Our runner retried once by default.
Helene (Infra): quick glance at metrics: heavy queueing, autoscaler triggered but pod start latencies ~50s. We have cold-start penalty hitting during the ramp. Also noticing GPU memory fragmentation and elevated KV cache miss rate which increases tail latency.
Ravi (Eng-Infra): Cluster has burst_pool=60 for hosted POC buckets. At this scale that's below needed capacity — I temporarily bumped burst_pool to 160 for the run. Also applied max_concurrency_per_instance=6 instead of 12 to reduce per-instance queuing. Will monitor.
Tess (Sales): For clarity on pricing: we absorb token costs for client-visible 5xxs during POC, so customers won't be billed. If you want guaranteed throughput for the demo, we can offer a short reserved capacity add-on (one-off invoice) to lock capacity and avoid throttling.
Priya (AcmeHealth): Appreciate that. We're concerned about failover behavior: if you hit capacity limits, does routing fallback to a smaller model automatically? We need to understand quality impact.
Luis (Eng): We can configure a routing policy per customer. Options: failover to redwood-13b-int8 (quantized) or downshift to redwood-7b. int8 keeps higher fidelity than 7b but may have slight numeric differences. For demo prompts you can expect near-parity; we'll run a quick eval.
Nora (AM): Security question from procurement: they want confirmation logs are access-restricted and retention set to 7 days for POC. Also need confirmation we won't persist full customer payloads beyond that.
Helene (Infra): Confirmed — for hosted POC we can set request log retention to 7 days and enable payload scrubbing. If they need absolute isolation, Private/VPC is available but requires lead time.
Priya (AcmeHealth): Ok keep hosted but enable scrubbing. Also can you annotate SLA numbers to reflect failovers? They want raw 5xx vs successful after fallback.
Ravi (Eng-Infra): We'll add a POC-level telemetry flag so console shows both raw upstream errors and post-routing success breakdown. It won't change the primary uptime metric but will surface fallback counts.
Luis (Eng): Quick mitigation steps applied: increased burst_pool->160, lowered max_concurrency->6, enabled ephemeral route_on_5xx to redwood-13b-int8 after 4 consecutive failures. Also shortened autoscale cooldown to 25s for this POC window to reduce cold-start exposure.
OpsBot: NOTICE: routing policy applied to tag poc-acme (route_on_5xx->redwood-13b-int8) at 14:22:07 UTC
Priya (AcmeHealth): Can you validate quality of int8 on our sample prompts before we run the next ramp at 14:45? Stakeholders want a quick pass/fail.
Luis (Eng): Will run a 50-sample diff on your prompt set and post a short summary within 20 minutes. If anything looks off we can instead downshift to redwood-7b for some paths.
Tess (Sales): I'll prepare a small addendum on pricing and note on 7-day retention for procurement.
Nora (AM): Logged ticket SEC-4022 to capture the retention and scrubbing agreement for the POC.
Priya (AcmeHealth): Thanks team. We'll hold the next ramp pending your sample results.
Luis (Eng): Posted quick eval: 50 prompts -> 48/50 within acceptance threshold vs fp32 baseline, two minor divergence cases flagged. Recommend proceed with int8 failover for the demo and keep the fallbacks visible in telemetry.
Priya (AcmeHealth): Sounds good. Please keep this channel for updates during the next ramp.
OpsBot: RESOLVED: burst_pool bump & routing policy in place at 14:27:33 UTC
